title: Azure DP-100: Data Scientist Associate Exam Guide
body:
Microsoft's DP-100 Azure Data Scientist Associate is the certification that separates data scientists who prototype in notebooks from those who architect and ship production ML systems on Azure. The exam covers the full machine learning lifecycle — from provisioning an Azure ML workspace and configuring compute targets through data ingestion via registered datastores, automated and custom model training, responsible AI evaluation, and MLOps deployment to managed endpoints. Microsoft revised the objectives significantly in late 2023, replacing the v1 SDK content with the Azure ML SDK v2 and CLI v2. Candidates whose study materials reference RunConfiguration objects or the legacy estimators API are studying for an exam that no longer exists.

The five domains weight heavily toward the engineering workflow. Domain 2 — exploring data and training models — accounts for 35–40% of the exam and covers AutoML configuration, custom command and sweep jobs, MLflow experiment tracking, hyperparameter tuning with Bayesian and random sampling, multi-step pipelines, and data asset patterns using mltable and uri_folder types. AutoML appears far more often than most candidates expect: the exam tests featurization options, primary metric selection per task type, and how to interpret the leaderboard rather than the underlying algorithms. Domain 3 covers Responsible AI: the exam expects you to read the fairness, interpretability, and error analysis panels in the Azure ML Responsible AI dashboard and draw the correct conclusion from cohort-level metrics — you do not need to implement the dashboard from code.

The DP-100 exam rewards scenario reasoning over service memorisation. You will not be asked to recite default node counts. You will be asked which compute type and sampling configuration handles 200 parallel hyperparameter sweep trials cost-efficiently with minimal idle time. The candidates who pass on first attempt spend 20–30 hours in an actual Azure ML workspace — provisioning compute, running AutoML jobs, building two-step pipelines, deploying to managed online endpoints, configuring blue/green traffic splits, and setting up data drift monitors — before taking the exam. Microsoft's $200 free trial credit is more than sufficient for a full four-week lab curriculum at approximately $20–40 in actual compute spend.

In the Azure certification stack, DP-100 sits at the associate tier alongside AZ-104 and AI-102. Many enterprise Azure ML job descriptions in 2026 explicitly list it as a requirement rather than a preference, driven by the overlap between Azure ML managed compute and Azure OpenAI fine-tuning and RAG pipeline infrastructure. Azure Data Scientists with DP-100 earn $120k–$140k at mid-level in the US; Senior Azure ML Engineers reach $140k–$165k; candidates who pair DP-100 with AI-102 or DP-203 command the strongest offers in 2026, as most enterprise roles now require both an ML engineering component and either a data engineering or applied AI component.
